NEW DELHI: Delhi environment minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa on Saturday hit out at the Punjab government over the killing of makeup artist and social media influencer Mad Sandhu, alleging that the state’s law and order was in the hands of the “mafia”.Sandhu, whose real name was Madhusudan, was shot dead by two unidentified motorcycle-borne men on Loharka Road in Amritsar at around 6pm on Saturday. Police said the attackers opened fire before fleeing the spot.Sandhu suffered two gunshot wounds and was rushed to a private hospital in critical condition, where he later died during treatment. An eyewitness said around two to three rounds were fired and that Sandhu was shot at close range.Reacting to the killing, Sirsa questioned the law and order situation in Punjab and alleged that several criminal networks were operating in the state under the Aam Aadmi Party government.“There is no law and order in Punjab. The law and order situation in Punjab is in the hands of the mafia. In Punjab, you receive only one piece of information every day,” Sirsa told ANI.“Otherwise, the police do not even register an FIR. If they are drug dealers, they are going around killing people. If they are mafia members, they are killing people. If there are gangsters, they are killing people. Social media influencer Mad Sandhu was shot dead and if even the Sarpanch of a village is not safe, and a former Sarpanch is not safe, then who is safe?”Sirsa further alleged that extortion gangs, mafia groups and the drug mafia were operating in Punjab.“During the tenure of the Aam Aadmi Party, gangs involved in extortion, the mafia, and the drug mafia are operating in Punjab. There is also a school mafia operating, where even if you raise your voice against problems in schools, you will be thrown out of the party,” he added.Madhusudan Sandhu was a makeup artist and social media influencer who regularly appeared on podcasts and digital platforms, where he spoke about make-up artistry, the film industry and gender issues. His content and fashion choices had also attracted criticism and abuse on social media.Sandhu had around 2.26 lakh followers on Instagram and had acted in the Punjabi film *Oye Bhole Oye*. A few months ago, a Nihang Sikh had objected to his social media content and clothing, saying his videos could have a negative impact on young people.Congress leader Raj Kumar Verka also criticised the AAP government over the killing and demanded Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann’s resignation, alleging that the government had failed to protect people.Amritsar MP Gurjeet Singh Aujla said Sandhu had been receiving threats for a long time and had spoken about them publicly on social media. He questioned why the threats had not been taken seriously and demanded an early arrest and a thorough investigation into who was behind the killing and why Sandhu had been threatened.
Article Summary: Sirsa questioned the law and order situation in punjab and alleged that several criminal networks were operating in the state. Sandhu, whose real name was madhusudan, was shot dead by two unidentified motorcycle-borne men on loharka road in amritsar.

Article Title: ‘If you manufacture a dictator, we will bury it’: Uddhav, Raj launch joint protest against CEC
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray and Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) chief Raj Thackeray on Sunday led a joint protest march in Mumbai against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, with participants demanding the cancellation of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Maharashtra.Addressing the gathering after the march, Uddhav Thackeray accused the government of attempting to create a dictatorship under the slogan of “Make in India”.“I think you will also remember that when Modi ji first became Prime Minister, he gave the slogan, “Make in India.” Remember? We accept that. But if, under “Make in India,” you are also going to manufacture a dictator in our country, then we have gathered here today to bury that dictatorship and put an end to it. Everything else under Make in India is fine. But if, in the name of Make in India, you are going to create a dictatorship, then consider that we have buried your dictatorship. ..”Speaking ahead of the protest, Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut said the demonstration was a collective response to what he alleged were attempts to undermine democratic institutions, electoral processes and the constitutional rights of citizens.“This protest is against the Hitler-rule prevailing in the country, hijacking elections, keeping the Election Commission and the Supreme Court in one's pocket, running a dictatorship, stealing votes, stealing elections, and poaching MPs and MLAs. This is a revolt against all that, much like the one in 1857,” he told reporters.Thackeray questioned the appointment process of Election Commissioners.“I have a question mark over the appointment of the Election Commissioners. The Election Commission should be appointed through an election. Earlier, there was a committee comprising the Chief Justice of India, the Prime Minister, and the Leader of the Opposition. They (the central government) removed the Chief Justice from this committee. In place of the Chief Justice, they appointed a minister chosen by the Prime Minister. That minister is Amit Shah. There are hearings after hearings in the courts, but there is no accountability.”Thackeray also questioned how Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar was appointed and alleged that powers related to citizenship rights were being exercised through the Election Commission.“The first question is: How was Gyanesh Kumar appointed? Does the Home Ministry have the power to cancel a person's citizenship rights? They are using that power through Gyanesh Kumar, and that is why we do not want Gyanesh Kumar. Earlier, it was 'India Against Corruption', and now it is 'India Against Vote Chors'... The BJP does not know how to run a government... The way you are running the government is not governance; it is revenge. ..”The march, dubbed the Virat Garjana Morcha (Grand Roar March), began at Metro Cinema and proceeded towards the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation headquarters in south Mumbai. State leaders of the Congress and the Sharad Pawar-led NCP (SP) also participated in the protest.The protesters demanded the removal or resignation of Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the SIR exercise.Party flags were not allowed during the march, with participants and supporters asked to carry only the national tricolour.
Article Summary: ‘make in india’ cannot mean manufacturing a dictator, says uddhav thackeray. Participants demand cancellation of the special intensive revision (sir) of electoral rolls in maharashtra. State leaders of the congress and the sharad pawar-led ncp (sp) also participated in the protest.

Article Title: Flydubai attack: Co-pilot identified as Hamam Alhamami was barred from flying in Oman over 'extremist views'
Article Text:
As per reports, Alhamami had repeatedly expressed support for Palestinians and hostility towards Israel. His alleged views are being examined as part of a wider investigation into possible Islamic radicalisation and terrorist motives

Removed from Oman Air training role

Pro-Palestinian material found among belongings

Questions over clearance for Tel Aviv flight

Who is Hamam Alhamami?

What happened aboard flydubai flight

The Omani co-pilot accused of attacking Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar aboard a flydubai flight to Tel Aviv has been identified as Hamam Alhamami. He was barred from flying in Oman over concerns about his alleged extremist views.Al Arabiya English, citing sources, reported that he had spent much of his time outside Oman, particularly in Syria, where he was allegedly influenced by extremist ideas before travelling to the UAE.The revelations follow a CNN report that Alhamami had been removed from a training role at Oman Air, Oman's national carrier, last year. However, he was later given another role at the airline, the report said, citing a regional diplomatic source familiar with the matter.Further reports have raised questions about Alhamami's alleged ideological views. i24 News, citing an Emirati source, reported that leaflets and publications from “Free Palestine” groups, along with other pro-Palestinian material, were found among his belongings.According to the report, Alhamami had repeatedly expressed support for Palestinians and hostility towards Israel. The report said investigators were examining the material as part of a broader probe into his alleged Islamic radicalisation and possible terrorist motives.The reports have also raised questions about how Alhamami was cleared to serve on a Tel Aviv-bound flight despite being an Omani citizen. Oman does not recognise Israel and has no diplomatic relations with the country.An Israeli official told CNN that several agencies, including Shin Bet, Mossad, the military and the Transportation Ministry, were investigating how Alhamami came to be part of the flight crew.According to the report, Alhamami is an Omani citizen. He was born in the United Arab Emirates to an Omani father and Syrian mother and spent several years of his life in the UAE. The Jerusalem Post, citing sources close to the investigation, reported that he did not hold a second nationality.CNN reported that Alhamami had worked for flydubai for only eight months. He had previously worked for Royal Air Maroc, Morocco's national carrier.Alhamami was transferred from Saudi Arabia to the UAE after the aircraft made an emergency landing in Tabuk. He is facing a terrorism investigation in the UAE.The September 30 incident took place aboard a flydubai flight travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv. Alhamami allegedly attacked Captain Machchhar inside the cockpit in what is being investigated as a possible terror-driven attempt to bring down the aircraft.The confrontation triggered a steep descent, with the aircraft dropping approximately 16,000 feet within two minutes before a hijacking distress signal was transmitted.Despite suffering severe injuries, Captain Machchhar resisted the attack and managed to open the cockpit door. Flight crew members and passengers then entered the cockpit and restrained Alhamami, allowing the crew to regain control of the aircraft.Two non-duty aviators who were travelling aboard the flight also helped assume control of the aircraft. The plane subsequently made an emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, with all 180 occupants disembarking safely.
Article Summary: Hamam alhamami is the omani co-pilot accused of attacking captain smit machchhar aboard a flydubai flight to tel aviv. He was barred from flying in oman over concerns about his alleged extremist views. Pro-palestinian material was found among his belongings, according to reports.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Wednesday said that he had a "productive conversation" with US President Donald Trump and reviewed bilateral cooperation between New Delhi and Washington in various sectors.In a social media post on X, PM Modi said the leaders agreed to maintain close engagement to take their Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership forward."Had a productive conversation with President Trump. Article Title: 'No deadline for Sheikh Hasina's return', says Indian high commissioner in Bangladesh
Article Text:
“At that point in time, Hasina was still the prime minister of Bangladesh. We had hardly any choice on that”, Trivedi said (Photo credit: AP).

Strained ties

NEW DELHI: The Indian high commissioner to Bangladesh on Saturday said Dhaka’s extradition request for ousted ex-Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina was being legally examined, so New Delhi could not state a deadline for her return.“Nobody can give you a timeframe (over Hasina’s return),” High commissioner Dinesh Trivedi remarked during a discussion organised by a Dhaka-based think tank. PTI reported.“Again and again, the government of India has replied to this that there is a process, and the process is legal, and it is well structured,” Trivedi added.Hasina sought asylum in India after a massive anti-establishment agitation led to the collapse of her government in August 2024.Trivedi said New Delhi had no role in Hasina’s extraction. She was escorted by a Bangladeshi military detachment from her residence and brought to India through a Bangladeshi aircraft.“At that point in time, Hasina was still the prime minister of Bangladesh. We had hardly any choice on that”, Trivedi said.Trivedi alleged the situation emerged because of “tragic circumstances” in Bangladesh, adding that such circumstances should never be repeated anywhere in the world.“What was our choice?” Trivedi asked, pointing at the uncertainty of the potential situation, had India denied entry to Hasina’s aircraft.India-Bangladesh ties severely deteriorated after Hasina sought asylum in Delhi.Hasina was replaced by an interim government led by Mohammad Yunus, which repeatedly called for her extraction from India.During that 18-month interim rule, Hasina was tried in absentia by a special tribunal and sentenced to death; her Awami League party was also disbanded.Following the February 12 elections, Tarique Rahman's Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) came to power. Its government endorsed the ban on Hasina's party and repeatedly renewed the demand for her extradition.However, relations never fully recovered despite a new government in Bangladesh.They were strained further when Hasina addressed a virtual press conference from New Delhi on 5 August 2026, the second anniversary of her removal from power. Bangladesh's foreign ministry had earlier said that the atmosphere for Rahman's visit had been "vitiated" by Hasina's virtual press interaction.India has maintained that it had no role in the media event and that it does not endorse anything said at the forum about the Bangladesh government.Rahman had declined the invitation to attend the BRICS outreach summit, while a separate bilateral invitation has been on hold since February.Despite the downturn in bilateral relations, Bangladesh's state minister for foreign affairs, Humaiun Kobir, said after meeting Trivedi on Tuesday that Dhaka was "positive" about progress in discussions on Rahman's proposed visit to India; PTI reported that no date has been fixed yet.
Article Summary: India-bangladesh ties severely deteriorated after hasina sought asylum in delhi. She was escorted by a bangladeshi military detachment from her residence and brought to india through an aircraft. Trivedi said new delhi had no role in hasina’s extraction.

NEW DELHI: India's role in efforts to find a negotiated end to the Russia-Ukraine war has gained greater prominence, with Kyiv describing an Indian proposal as the most comprehensive among four initiatives currently under discussion and saying New Delhi has, for the first time, indicated its willingness to play an active mediating role.Ukrainian foreign minister Andrii Sybiha recently said Ukraine was prepared to consider both an energy and agricultural truce in the Black Sea, while also remaining open to an unconditional ceasefire along the line of contact."We have four proposals. The most comprehensive is India's proposal. For the first time, India has signalled its willingness to play a role," Sybiha said during a press briefing, according to RBC Ukraine.According to Sybiha, four proposals are currently being considered in diplomatic efforts surrounding the war.India's proposal was described by the Ukrainian foreign minister as the most comprehensive.Türkiye and Egypt have separately proposed a grain and agricultural truce in the Black Sea, while the United States has put forward an energy truce proposal.The agricultural and maritime component is particularly important for Egypt, which relies on Ukrainian grain for roughly a third of its supply, according to RBC Ukraine.The US proposal on an energy truce was also discussed during a meeting between Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and US President Donald Trump.Kyiv has conveyed its own approach to its partners and wants the energy and Black Sea components to be treated as an interconnected package.Sybiha said the energy component would require a complete halt to attacks on energy infrastructure, including port facilities.Ukraine has also expressed readiness for an unconditional ceasefire along the line of contact. Sybiha said such a ceasefire could potentially emerge from a meeting between Zelenskyy and Russian President Vladimir Putin.The US is currently working actively on this diplomatic track, according to the Ukrainian foreign minister.The latest Ukrainian position builds on India's earlier engagement with Kyiv over restoring safe navigation in the Black Sea.During last month's UN General Assembly-related engagements, Zelenskyy said Egypt, India and Türkiye had put forward options for a maritime truce between Russia and Ukraine."We are waiting for Russia's response. Ukraine is ready ... to ensure safe shipping and food security in the Black Sea if Russia is ready to take real steps towards de-escalation too. We have to start somewhere," Zelenskyy said at the time.India has been engaging with both Moscow and Kyiv while advocating dialogue and diplomacy.External affairs minister S Jaishankar had said India was in continuous contact with both sides and was exploring ideas that could help mitigate and eventually end the conflict."If India can be of any help, in any manner, we are there," Jaishankar said during his visit to Kyiv last month.During that visit, Jaishankar met Zelenskyy and Sybiha, with discussions covering peace efforts, bilateral cooperation, Black Sea navigation and global food security.Sybiha had also said Ukraine valued India's engagement in efforts to restore freedom of navigation in the Black Sea."Restoring freedom of navigation is critical for global food security. Ukraine is ready to play a constructive role and we value India’s engagement," he said in a post on X.While Ukraine has indicated its readiness to consider multiple limited ceasefire arrangements, Russia's response remains central to whether the proposals can move forward.Sybiha's comments come amid differing assessments in Europe over Moscow's willingness to enter substantive peace negotiations.German Chancellor Friedrich Merz recently said Russia was not currently interested in genuine peace negotiations, while German foreign minister Johann Wadephul has expressed expectations that talks to end the war could begin in the near future.The Kremlin had previously said there were no prerequisites for moving towards a broader peace negotiating track while maintaining that Russia remained open to talks."For now, there are no prerequisites for moving on to a peaceful negotiating track, although we, as the Russian side, remain open to peace talks," Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said.Ukraine's latest position therefore places several limited ceasefire proposals, covering energy infrastructure, Black Sea shipping and agricultural supplies, alongside the possibility of a broader unconditional ceasefire along the line of contact.India's proposal is being considered alongside those initiatives, with Sybiha describing it as the most comprehensive and saying New Delhi has now signalled its readiness to play a role in the process.
Article Summary: India's role in efforts to find a negotiated end to the russia-ukraine war has gained greater prominence. Kyiv has described an indian proposal as the most comprehensive among four initiatives currently under discussion. New delhi has indicated its willingness to play an active mediating role.

NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs on Saturday summoned the Chargé d'Affaires of the Pakistan high commission to lodge a strong protest over what it described as the continued facilitation of illegal cross-border infiltration from Pakistan.It also rejected as “baseless and motivated” Pakistan’s allegations over an October 2 incident in the Ferozepur sector of Punjab along the International Border.MEA said that Pakistan was informed that three individuals had entered Indian territory and continued moving towards the border fence despite repeated warnings from the BSF to return. The force subsequently engaged them after they were assessed to pose an imminent security threat."The Pakistani side was informed that three individuals infiltrated into Indian territory and despite multiple warnings by BSF to return to Pakistan, continued to move towards the border fence. The BSF was compelled to engage them for posing an imminent security threat," MEA said in a statement.MEA said the incident was part of a repeated pattern of cross-border movement by armed narcotics syndicates operating from Pakistan.Islamabad was urged to investigate such infiltration and drug-smuggling activities, including the alleged involvement of Pakistani border forces, and take appropriate corrective measures."This incident highlights a clear pattern of repeated cross-border movement by armed narcotics syndicates operating from Pakistan. Government of Pakistan was urged to investigate these cross-border infiltration, drug smuggling activities and the complicity of Pakistan Border Guarding forces therein, and to take appropriate remedial measures," it said."Pakistan was further urged to ensure respect for the sanctity of the International Border, strictly observe relevant bilateral arrangements, mandate its forces to exercise effective control to prevent unauthorized movement from its side, and take definitive measures to prevent the recurrence of such incidents," it added.

Article Title: Russia to take 70,000 Indian skilled workers this year, Jaishankar tells panel
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar on Saturday briefed a parliamentary consultative committee on India's "multifaceted" engagement with Russia, covering bilateral trade, investment and energy cooperation as well as New Delhi's diplomatic efforts to contribute towards ending the Ukraine conflict.Chairing the meeting on India-Russia relations, Jaishankar also informed members that Russia has agreed to take around 70,000 Indian skilled workers this year, particularly in construction and logistics, people familiar with the discussions said, according to news agency PTI.Jaishankar said India and Russia share an ambition to expand bilateral trade in a more balanced manner, including by increasing Indian exports to Russia across seven sectors — automobiles, pharmaceuticals, food, marine products, engineering goods, chemicals and textiles.The minister highlighted various areas of bilateral engagement, including trade, investments, energy, connectivity, culture and people-to-people ties, according to a social media post by Jaishankar.The discussions also covered an India-Eurasian Economic Union Free Trade Agreement, the Chennai-Vladivostok corridor, the International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC) and the Northern Sea Route.On energy cooperation, Jaishankar said India's priority was to safeguard the interests of Indian consumers."Our approach is to maintain multiple sources of supply," he said, according to people familiar with the meeting.The government has also been seeking to expand opportunities for Indian workers in Russia.The Ukraine conflict also featured prominently in the discussions, with Jaishankar apprising the panel of India's position and recent diplomatic efforts to support dialogue and diplomacy.In his social media post, Jaishankar said he highlighted India's "active support to dialogue & diplomacy to end the Ukraine conflict".The minister referred to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's August 31 meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Bishkek, where the PM said that "endless war must now give way to end of war".Jaishankar travelled to Ukraine last month and subsequently met the foreign ministers of Ukraine and Russia in New York on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly. During those engagements, he conveyed India's readiness to assist efforts to bring the conflict to an end, people familiar with the meeting said."If India can be of any help in any manner to bring the war to an end, it is ready to do so," Jaishankar said in his conversations.Putin's recent remarks at the Valdai Club in Moscow were also discussed. He had said Prime Minister Modi "has very good ideas for finding mutually acceptable solutions" to bring peace.Ukrainian foreign minister Andrii Sybiha's remarks appreciating India's efforts were also noted during the meeting.Jaishankar also briefed the committee on the government's efforts to secure the release of Indian nationals serving in the Russian military.The government has engaged with Russian authorities, including at the highest levels, for the early discharge of such individuals, the people cited above said.So far, around 140 Indian nationals have been discharged, while India is in touch with Russian authorities regarding the whereabouts of 55 Indian nationals who are reportedly working for the Russian Arm.The government has also been taking action against agents who recruit Indians for such roles, with members being briefed about the risks faced by Indian citizens joining the Russian Army.The parliamentary committee meeting thus covered India's economic and energy engagement with Russia alongside its diplomatic efforts on Ukraine and its continuing efforts to secure the release of Indian nationals serving in the Russian military.
Article Summary: S jaishankar briefed a parliamentary consultative committee on india's "multifaceted" engagement with russia. The minister highlighted trade, investments, energy, connectivity, culture and people-to-people ties. He also briefed the committee on the government's efforts to secure the release of indian nationals serving in the russian military.

Article Title: 'He prayed before attack': Machchhar tells Netanyahu chilling flydubai cockpit ordeal
Article Text:

Netanyahu invites Machchhar to Israel

Flydubai pilot Captain Smit Machchhar spoke to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu where he described the incidents that unfolded inside the cockpit. He also described how he managed to open the cockpit door despite suffering repeated blows to his head. Netanyahu praised his courage and said he had "saved so many souls".Machchhar told Netanyahu that the flight had initially been normal. The co-pilot then wanted to play a game that he said many locals play. While Machchhar was looking towards the front of the aircraft, he suddenly felt a heavy blow to the back of his head.Machchhar also told Netanyahu that the co-pilot had wanted to pray before the attack. He said he looked towards the front of the cockpit out of respect while the co-pilot prayed."...while he was praying, out of respect, I was just looking at the front and not at the back, and suddenly, after, I would say about four-five minutes, there was a big blow to the back of my head."My first thought was that there was a catastrophic damage to the aircraft and something is not right," Machchhar said.He said the blows continued and he soon realised that the aircraft had not been damaged. Instead, the co-pilot was attacking him."And that's when I realised that it's not the aircraft, it's the other guy who was in the cockpit with me," he said.Machchhar said the initial blows left his vision severely blurred, making it difficult for him to understand what was happening. He then felt the aircraft sharply descending."My memory is still in bits and pieces right now," he told Netanyahu.The pilot also recalled trying to open the cockpit door once, but said the co-pilot shut it again. He later found himself lying on the cockpit floor as he heard the aircraft moving rapidly and passengers screaming.Machchhar said he then realised he had to make one final attempt to reach the door."And as I was telling the ambassador here, that I had that one last fight left in me that, you know, call it personal or call it for people," he said. "But let's say I did it that if I don't do it, I'm going to die."He said he pushed himself towards the door and managed to open it. Crew members and others outside then took control of the situation."And thankfully people were waiting to bounce back, took over the control and the rest is what you know, sir," Machchhar said.Netanyahu asked Machchhar how he had managed to open the cockpit door when the co-pilot was preventing access.Machchhar explained that the door has a twist mechanism on the inside and can normally be opened from outside only using a code. His colleagues outside the cockpit were trying to enter the code, but the attacker was preventing the door from being opened."The only way to open the door was to reach the knob and like any other knob, just to twist it open and it opens on its own," Machchhar said."There is no pin, but yes, the door, it was, it was a short, quick twist, but the point was to reach to that point, to reach to that place."Once he reached the knob, Machchhar said he was able to twist it open.Netanyahu repeatedly praised Machchhar during the conversation, calling him a hero of India, Israel and the world."I, frankly, I'm amazed at your courage, at your coolness of judgement under impossible conditions," Netanyahu said.He said Machchhar's actions had helped save lives and described the incident as an example of how courage could overcome violence."You're a hero of Israel. You're a hero of India. You're a hero of the entire world," Netanyahu said.The Israeli prime minister also said Machchhar would be welcomed in Israel and invited him and his family to visit.Netanyahu said he wanted Machchhar and PM Modi to light a celebratory flame at Israel's next Independence Day ceremony. He described the honour as one usually reserved for Israeli citizens."I really would like them to bear a celebratory flame. It's our highest honour that we give in our Independence Day. It's usually reserved for Israeli citizens," Netanyahu said."But I think here in this case, all the citizens of Israel will, will embrace you. They do now and they will then too."Machchhar thanked Netanyahu and said he looked forward to meeting him in Israel.Netanyahu ended the conversation by wishing the pilot a speedy recovery and saying his visit to Israel would be "memorable and historic".
Article Summary: Captain smit machchhar spoke to israeli prime minister benjamin netanyahu. He described how he managed to open the cockpit door despite suffering repeated blows to his head. Netanyahu praised his courage and said he had "saved so many souls"machchhar said the initial blows left his vision severely blurred, making it difficult for him to understand what was happening.

NEW DELHI: Union finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman on Saturday said that amid uncertainty, “now a standing condition” of the global economy, national security requires structural autonomy in strategic inputs, as strategic resource security sits at the centre of macroeconomic policy.Besides, she argued for private investment to lead the cycle, including in research and innovation and skilling to prepare people for a changing world of work, while asserting that global financial architecture should reflect where growth was coming from.“We need to keep building resilience as we go along; it’s not a one-time exercise. To replace fragile single-source dependencies with domestic operational depth, the government has launched programmes focused on critical minerals and rare earths, semiconductors and small modular nuclear reactors.She said for India, resilience means building upon the structural foundations laid over the past decade such as entrepreneurial growth, focusing on efficient last-mile delivery, infrastructure creation and managing prices, essential supplies and external pressures. “The test of the coming years will again be partly invisible: the shocks India absorbs without disruption to households and enterprises.”The evidence of resilience lies in the counterfactual, in the outcomes that did not materialise, such as an inflation spiral that did not take hold, queues that did not form at the fuel outlets, banking stress that did not surface and a fiscal correction that was never forced. “These counterfactuals deserve as much attention from economists as the headline growth rate,” she added.Talking about open, predictable and rule-based global economic relationships, Sitharaman said nations should engage with one another through dialogue and negotiated agreements, rather than allowing geopolitical differences to become barriers to trade and investment.

Article Title: Hormuz blocked, but Gulf crude shipments at pre-war level
Article Text:
Of the remaining 60% that physically crossed Hormuz, most was moved using shuttle tankers, Emmanuel Belostrino, head of global crude and geopolitical market data at Kpler, said in his analysis.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Crude via other routes made up the difference

325 million barrels released from oil reserves: IEA

Disruptions to energy supplies through the Strait of Hormuz notwithstanding, crude shipments from the West Asian Gulf region, excluding Iran, have returned to pre-war levels as countries cut dependence on oil tankers to navigate through the choked strait. According to maritime intelligence and research firm Kpler, at least 16.5 million barrels per day (mbd) of crude left the region between Sept 1 and 28, matching the prewar average. During the peak of the West Asia war in March, the average was 10.5 mbd.While 83% of the region’s crude crossed Hormuz before the war, 40% was exported in Sept through pipelines in Saudi Arabia and the UAE without crossing the key chokepoint.Of the remaining 60% that physically crossed Hormuz, most was moved using shuttle tankers, Emmanuel Belostrino, head of global crude and geopolitical market data at Kpler, said in his analysis.Belostrino said more than 70% of the crude that crossed the Strait of Hormuz in Aug changed tankers offshore in the Gulf of Oman.Confirmed crude crossings were still more than a quarter below the pre-war level, but volumes moving through alternative routes had more than doubled and made up almost exactly the difference. Saudi pushed more crude through the east-west pipeline to Yanbu, with loadings rising from 0.8 mbd before the war to 4.3 mbd in June. UAE sent crude through the Abu Dhabi crude oil pipeline to Fujairah, where loadings rose from 1.1 mbd to 2.7 mbd.The International Energy Agency said member countries had released 325 million barrels of oil and oil products from strategic reserves, out of 400 million barrels pledged in March.
Article Summary: Crude shipments from the west asian gulf region, excluding iran, have returned to pre-war levels as countries cut dependence on oil tankers. At least 16.5 million barrels per day (mbd) of crude left the region between sept 1 and 28, matching the prewar average.

Article Title: Indians live longer than Pakistanis, lag Bangladeshis, says WHO
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Indians can expect to live longer than their counterparts in Pakistan, but have shorter lives than people in Bangladesh, the US and Canada, according to the latest World Health Organization estimates.India's life expectancy at birth was 71 years in 2023, compared with 68.2 years in Pakistan, 72.7 years in Bangladesh, 78.5 years in the US and 81.4 years in Canada. But living longer does not necessarily mean living more years in good health. India's healthy life expectancy was 60.6 years in 2023, compared with 60.5 in 2019. It had fallen to 58.4 years in 2021 before recovering to 60.2 years in 2022. The figures are part of WHO's Global Health Estimates, released Friday, covering life expectancy, healthy life expectancy, causes of death and disease burden from 2000 to 2023. WHO said global life expectancy recovered close to pre-pandemic levels, while healthy life expectancy has recovered more slowly.For India, the difference is particularly visible over the pandemic years. Life expectancy fell from 70.5 years in 2019 to 68.1 years in 2021 before rising to 70.5 years in 2022 and 71 years in 2023. In just two years, India regained 2.9 years of expected lifespan.Healthy life expectancy, however, recovered by only 2.2 years, from 58.4 years in 2021 to 60.6 years in 2023, leaving it just 0.1 year above the 2019 level.The gap is also visible among older Indians. At age 60, a person could expect another 18.8 years of life in 2023, compared with 18.4 years in 2019. But 13.7 of those years were expected to be lived in full health, up from 13.4 years in 2019.India’s disease profile has changed sharply. Communicable diseases, such as tuberculosis and diarrhoeal infections, can spread from person to person, while non-communicable diseases (NCDs), such as heart disease, stroke and diabetes, are generally long-term conditions.In 2000, communicable diseases accounted for nearly 62% of the combined death rate from the country’s 10 leading causes, while NCDs accounted for 34%. By 2023, the pattern had reversed, with NCDs accounting for nearly 75% and communicable diseases 16% of the combined death rate from the top 10 causes. The rest was from injuries.The shift is evident in the leading causes. In 2000, tuberculosis and diarrhoeal diseases topped the list, with 92.4 and 87.8 deaths per 100,000 population. By 2023, ischaemic heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, stroke and diabetes were among the leading causes, with rates of 138.5, 83.19, 74.8 and 49.01, respectively. Yet infectious diseases remain a significant burden, with diarrhoeal diseases, tuberculosis and lower respiratory infections still among India’s top 10 causes of death in 2023.Globally, the shift towards chronic diseases is also pronounced. NCDs accounted for 74% of deaths in 2023, up from 58% in 2000, while eight of the world’s 10 leading causes of death were NCDs. Global life expectancy reached 73.3 years in 2023, almost back to the 73.4 years recorded in 2019, while healthy life expectancy stood at 62.8 years, still 0.4 years below its 2019 level.
Article Summary: India's life expectancy at birth was 71 years in 2023, compared with 68.2 years in pakistan, 72.7 years in bangladesh, 78.5 years in the us and 81.4 years in canada. In 2 years from 2021, india regained 2.9 years of expected lifespan: who.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has invited Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar to light a flame at Israel's Independence Day event. Speaking to Machchhar, he called him a "hero" of Israel, India and the entire world for foiling an alleged attempt to crash an Israel-bound flydubai flight.Netanyahu spoke to the 38-year-old pilot on Saturday while Machchhar was undergoing treatment at a hospital in the UAE. During the emotional conversation, Machchhar recounted how he was attacked by his co-pilot inside the cockpit and revealed new details about the incident."It's our highest honour that we give on our Independence Day. It's usually reserved for Israeli citizens, but I think here in this case, all the citizens of Israel will embrace you. They do now, and they will then too. So we hope to see you very soon in Israel," Netanyahu told Machchhar.The Israeli Prime Minister's office later said on X, "You are a hero for Israel, India, and the entire world. I invite Prime Minister Narendra Modi and you to light a flame on Israeli Independence Day.""During the emotional conversation that took place this evening, the Prime Minister asked Captain Machchhar how it all started, and Machchhar revealed new details about the terrifying moments in the cockpit," the post said.Machchhar told Netanyahu that the co-pilot had wanted to pray before the attack. He said he looked towards the front of the cockpit out of respect while the co-pilot prayed."...while he was praying, out of respect, I was just looking at the front and not at the back, and suddenly, after, I would say about four-five minutes, there was a big blow to the back of my head."My first thought was that there was catastrophic damage to the aircraft and something was not right. But then after that, the blows kept coming one after the other, and that's when I realised that it's not the aircraft, it's the other guy who was in the cockpit with me," Machchhar said.Netanyahu praised the pilot for his actions during the incident."You saved so many souls. I think you saved something bigger. You saved the spirit of the world...It's something that is being justly hailed around the world. You're a hero of Israel. You're a hero of India. You're a hero of the entire world," Netanyahu told Machchhar."You know, I guess it's a twist of fate, and a twist of faith, and what you did is remarkable. I heard, of course, from the Israeli passengers what transpired after that, and you're a great hero, and you were accompanied by heroes, and you saved the day," he said.Netanyahu also told Machchhar he was "amazed at his courage" and "at your coolness of judgment under impossible conditions."The incident took place on Wednesday aboard flydubai flight FZ1073, which was carrying 174 passengers to Israel. Machchhar was allegedly attacked by his co-pilot with a crash axe, an emergency tool kept inside the cockpit.The aircraft transmitted emergency signals and made a rapid descent of more than 17,000 feet, from 34,000 feet. It eventually made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia. The descent was so extreme that part of the aircraft's rudder was reportedly torn away.The co-pilot has been identified as Omani national Hamam al-Hammami, according to a Wall Street Journal report citing people familiar with the matter.Machchhar received initial treatment in Tabuk before being shifted to Abu Dhabi for continued medical care.The co-pilot of a Flydubai flight, Hamam al-Hammami, allegedly attacked the captain with a crash axe inside the cockpit and attempted to take control of the aircraft. UAE described the incident as a terrorist attack.UAE prosecutor general Hamad Saif Al Shamsi said the co-pilot launched the attack during Wednesday's flight and tried to seize control of the aircraft. The incident was subsequently classified by UAE authorities as an attempted terrorist attack.

Article Title: 'Recovering well': MEA provides update on flydubai pilot Smit Machchhar attacked by co-pilot
Article Text:

Co-pilot allegedly tried to seize control

UAE investigation underway

NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs (MEA) on Saturday said flydubai pilot Captain Smit Machchhar was recovering well after he was attacked by his co-pilot during a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv.The MEA said Machchhar remained under “excellent medical care” and that it was in touch with his family and local authorities.“Indian braveheart Capt. Smit remains under excellent medical care & is recovering well. We are in touch with his family & local authorities, extending support for a speedy recovery. Our thanks to UAE gov. for their care. We join well-wishers in praying for his good health,” Indian embassy in UAE said in a post on X.The attack took place on September 30 aboard flydubai flight FZ1073, which was bound for Tel Aviv. According to the UAE's state news agency WAM, citing attorney general counsellor Hamad Saif al-Shamsi, the Omani co-pilot, Hamam al-Hammami, attacked Machchhar with a cockpit crash axe while attempting to take control of the aircraft.The UAE attorney general said al-Hammami “attempted to carry out a terrorist act” and sought to seize command of the aircraft's piloting instruments while the plane was airborne.The assault triggered a violent struggle inside the cockpit, during which the aircraft reportedly lost about 16,000 feet in two minutes, according to reports on the incident. Machchhar, despite sustaining serious injuries, fought back and managed to unlock the cockpit door.Crew members, passengers and two off-duty pilots then entered the cockpit and helped overpower the co-pilot, allowing the aircraft to be stabilised.The flight subsequently made an emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. All 180 people on board safely disembarked.A crash axe is a standard emergency tool kept in aircraft cockpits and is designed to help pilots cut through aircraft materials during emergencies.The UAE authorities are investigating the incident to establish the circumstances, motive and possible connections linked to the attack.“The conclusive findings will be made public immediately once all mandatory legal and administrative steps have successfully concluded,” al-Shamsi said, according to WAM.Investigators are also examining physical and digital evidence as part of the probe.Reports raise questions over co-pilot's backgroundMedia reports have also raised questions about al-Hammami's background and previous aviation career.According to sources cited by CBS News and Al Arabiya English, al-Hammami had previously undergone pilot training with Oman Air. He was reportedly moved to desk duties after authorities detected visits to radical websites and later resigned around 2024. Reports also said he had previously been barred from flying in Oman over extremist concerns linked to an earlier stay in Syria.After moving to Dubai, he was hired by flydubai, with reports raising questions about whether the Omani government was formally involved in his background checks.CNN also reported that posts appeared on a LinkedIn profile associated with al-Hammami after the incident, including cockpit footage of an El Al aircraft and images of Al-Qaeda figures. The authenticity and circumstances surrounding those posts remain part of the broader scrutiny of the case.The UAE authorities have not yet released their final findings on the motive behind the attack or the circumstances that led to al-Hammami's actions. The investigation remains ongoing.
Article Summary: Machchhar remains under medical care following the cockpit assault on september 30. Uae authorities have not yet released their final findings on the motive behind the attack or the circumstances that led to hamam al-hammami's actions. Media reports have also raised questions about his background and previous aviation career.

NEW DELHI: The Congress on Monday questioned Prime Minister Narendra Modi for not addressing rising inflation in his Mann Ki Baat radio address, accusing him of being “blissfully unconcerned” about the issue.The opposition party’s attack came a day after PM Modi addressed the nation in the 138th episode of Mann Ki Baat.“The brunt of inflation is no longer confined just to the kitchen, yet the Prime Minister remains blissfully unconcerned, beating his drum away. Vegetables are getting more expensive by the day, with onion prices soaring 48.27% in August. Items such as air conditioners, TVs and refrigerators are also set to become more expensive. Household savings are steadily declining, while family debt is mounting. In such a scenario, how is the common family supposed to meet its needs?” Congress MP Jairam Ramesh wrote on X.Ramesh questioned why PM Modi continues to “sermonise” in the Mann Ki Baat series instead of addressing the public’s concerns.“In his ‘Mann Ki Baat’ radio series, the Prime Minister keeps sermonising on various issues, but when will he address the country’s most pressing concern—inflation? When will he care about the public’s worries? The public is already beleaguered by rising prices, and there’s no relief coming from the government.How on earth is the average family supposed to manage its budget? How long will the middle class and the poor have their backs broken like this?” the Rajya Sabha MP asked.According to the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation’s (MoSPI) Consumer Price Index (CPI) release, retail inflation, based on the 2024=100 CPI, stood at 4.82% in August, up from 4.45% in July. Food inflation, measured by the Consumer Food Price Index (CFPI), rose to 5.95% in August from 5.52% in July. The August figures are provisional.Official data showed that onion inflation surged from 22.54% in July to 48.27% in August. Ginger recorded inflation of 73.82%, while garlic inflation stood at 43.60%. In contrast, tomato prices fell 31.09% year-on-year, while potato prices declined 13.14%.MoSPI data showed inflation in the combined food and beverages category at 5.66% in August. Transport inflation stood at 4.60 percent, education services at 3.73%, while restaurants and accommodation services recorded inflation of 8.38%. Personal care, social protection and miscellaneous goods and services registered inflation of 15.17%.The CPI data was compiled from price information collected across 1,407 urban markets, including online markets, and 1,465 villages nationwide. MoSPI reported a 100% response rate from both rural and urban markets in August.According to MoSPI, the next CPI data, covering September, is scheduled to be released on October 12.
